messages:
alex: Quick question — running into weird behavior with envFrom + optional secret in our Helm chart. In a production overlay we intentionally set secretName: null and helm template renders:
```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: <nil>
```
Pod fails to start. Is this expected or should chart guard against empty/null secret names?

morgan: Hmm yeah that will blow up. Helm's tpl/default can help but it depends on how you pass values. Are you doing `{{ .Values.secretName }}` directly in the template?

alex: Yup, simple template: `envFrom: - secretRef: name: {{ .Values.secretName }}`. I expected it to omit the block if secretName is null but it inserts `<nil>`.

sam: Use an `if` guard. e.g.:
```gotpl
{{- if .Values.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secretName | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
That way nothing renders when secretName is empty.

morgan: Another pattern is to default to empty string and check `ne`:
```gotpl
{{- $s := default "" .Values.secretName -}}
{{- if ne $s "" }}
  envFrom:
    - secretRef:
        name: {{ $s | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

priya: FWIW we hit an edge-case where external secret controllers create an empty secret (no keys) and envFrom still causes issues even if name exists. In that case you might prefer explicit env entries so you can reference a particular key: `env: - name: FOO valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: my-secret key: foo` — then Kubernetes gives clearer errors/logs.

alex: @priya good point. For our use-case the secret is truly optional so I'd rather omit envFrom entirely if the name is not set. Will add the `if .Values.secretName` guard.

sam: Also: if you want to be extra safe at template-time you can use the `lookup` function to check cluster state (only works when rendering against a live cluster):
```gotpl
{{- $s := .Values.secretName -}}
{{- if and $s (lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace $s) }}
  envFrom:
    - secretRef:
        name: {{ $s | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
Note: `helm template` locally won't have the secret so unit tests might fail unless you mock.

infra-bot: CI: `helm lint` failed on branch alex/optional-secret — template: envFrom.secretRef.name: invalid value "" (chart-templates/containers.yaml:45) :warning:

morgan: For linting we add a unit test (helm unittest) that renders with `secretName: null` and assert that `envFrom` is not present. Cheap and prevents regressions.

alex: Plan: open PR with `if .Values.secretName` guard + helm-unittest case. Will also replace any direct `{{ .Values.secretName }}` uses with `default`/guard. cc @eng-platform :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks — if you want I can review the PR quickly and check our production overlays that set `secretName: ""` vs `null`. We have a mix.

alex: Awesome, please do. I'll normalize overlays too.

morgan: One last note — document this in chart README: "secretName is optional; omit to disable envFrom" so future folks don't reintroduce `<nil>` patterns.

alex: Will add README blurb in the PR.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INF-3421 "helm: guard envFrom when secretName not set" (assigned to alex)
